messages:
sam_k: Hey team — used an urgent care on 2026-03-20 while traveling and realized my insurance card was missing. Clinic billed me $220 and the carrier denied for 'no member ID presented'. I have the paid receipt. Anyone have a quick path to reimbursement?

lee_peopleops: Sorry that happened @sam_k. Which plan are you on (PPO/HMO)? If PPO you can usually self-submit a claim with proof of payment. If HMO its more limited.

sam_k: Redwood Core PPO. The clinic said they can re-file if I provide member ID or a signed form. I don't have the physical card.

tasha_benefits: Ok steps: 1) Grab a digital ID from the carrier portal (Member > ID card > Download PDF). 2) Ask clinic billing to re-submit the claim with the member ID and attach the paid receipt. 3) If clinic won't re-file, file an OON claim via the carrier portal: attach itemized receipt, proof of payment, and short cover letter explaining lost card. 4) If still denied, submit an appeal referencing emergency/urgent care.

mike_billing: Most clinics can update the claim if you sign a release. I can send a brief clinic-facing template if you want to have them re-bill.

lee_peopleops: DM me and Ill request a replacement card PDF from the carrier and upload it to you. Also Finance can offer a short-term advance if youd like — upload receipt to Expensify with tag "health-advance".

finance_bot: [automated] Finance advance policy: one-off payouts require original receipt + brief justification. Typical review time 1-3 business days.

sam_k: Thanks. @lee_peopleops please DM the PDF. @mike_billing yes please share the clinic re-bill template. If carrier makes me appeal I'll use the template. I'll update thread once re-bill or claim processed.
